## A 2nd+ concurrent orchestration now gets a named, reusable workspace instead of a numbered throwaway one

Opening a second (or third, or fourth) concurrent orchestration against the same root checkout already isolated it into its own git clone. What that clone was *called*, and what happened to it afterward, didn't track how this repository's own workflow actually wants to use them.

**The workspace directory is now named after the orchestration itself.** Previously the directory came from a separate "Worktree slug" field on the New Pane form, auto-generated as `<repo>-orchestrator-1`, `<repo>-orchestrator-2`, and so on if left blank — sprawl that carried no relationship to the orchestration's own typed Name. That field is gone. The workspace directory is now derived directly from the Name you type, the same Name that already has to be unique among your live orchestrations.

**Reopening an orchestration under the same Name resumes its existing workspace instead of refusing.** A closed orchestration's workspace — including any uncommitted changes and local-only commits sitting in it — is still there the next time you open a new orchestration under that same Name, and it is reattached rather than starting fresh. Resuming never fetches or merges anything into your work automatically beyond a read-only check of how far ahead or behind `origin` you are; nothing about your tree changes without your say-so.

**A named workspace is never deleted just because its tab closed.** That was already true in practice for isolated clones, and it now holds as a deliberate guarantee rather than an accident of nothing trying.

**Two safety properties worth knowing about.** A Name that would produce the same on-disk workspace as another live orchestration's Name is refused rather than silently sharing that orchestration's directory. And resuming a workspace whose git history no longer looks like it came from this project's root checkout is refused too, rather than quietly reattaching to the wrong repository.
